title: HTML Basics
summary: Every page starts with a document shell: doctype, html, head, and body. Then you add headings, paragraphs, and links.
objectives: Recognize the basic HTML document shell
Add a heading, a paragraph, and a link

content.md: HTML is the **structure** of a web page. CSS is style. JavaScript is behavior. This lesson is only structure.
A page starts with `<!DOCTYPE html>` so the browser uses modern HTML. Then `<html>` wraps everything, `<head>` holds metadata (title, charset), and `<body>` holds what the reader sees.

items: `<h1>` — the page title on the page itself
`<a href="...">` — a link. `href` is the destination

content.md: Visible content goes in `<body>`. The tab label goes in `<title>` inside `<head>`.

children.md: Without `<!DOCTYPE html>`, some browsers switch to quirks mode and layout rules from the 1990s. Always include it as the first line.
